Stephanie / Ben —

Reviewed Bluepine’s v2 redline and drafted a short digest (see attached redline-summary-notes.pdf). Key takeaways:

- SCCs: Redwood is prepared to sign the 2021/2023-style SCCs but we will attach our standard processor exhibit. The customer wants a static subprocessor list; our standard position is a notification + objection right.
- Transfer-impact addendum: Bluepine’s draft is broader than our operational model — they request a categorical limitation on transfers to certain non-EU regions. Ops has indicated we can support VPC-only routing for EU tenants but cannot commit to contractual locational guarantees for all workloads.
- Liability & indemnity: Bluepine tightened liability caps tied to data classification. Recommend we push a defined carveout for model output and third-party models to avoid open-ended exposure.

Action items I recommend:
- Commercial to confirm whether customer timeline (sign by Nov 14) is firm and if any Order Form start date is sensitive to the DPA signoff.
- Legal to propose replacement language: (a) static subprocessor list accepted only if customer agrees to quarterly updates/notifications; (b) transfer-impact clause limited to operational commitments (routing preferences) not absolute guarantees.

I’ve attached a short redline with proposed edits and tracked notes. Happy to join the call tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
